chapter: Brown's Band in Chicago and New York
title: Wagon advertising, prize fights and theaters
summary: Where the band played: wagons for prize fights, the Winter Garden, the Dauphine Theater.

blocks.x: That I don't remember of ever playing up there. What about prize fights? Well, yes. We played on the wagon for prize fights. You never played in the fight? In the inside? No, there wasn't any reason to have a band in there at that time. Oh, yeah. I've heard Shillings, any number of times. Well, that must have been later on. I mean, because, uh... Oh, it was later on. I would say it was maybe around 1920, around that... Oh, yeah. That was later. I remember that, uh, later on they played in, but I don't ever remember playing inside, even when Lou Rose had the Winter Garden. I used to put the fights on there. Yeah. That's on Barone Street. Yeah. That's right. We never did play in there, and that was a good place. They had a big stage where the, uh, ring was set up, and it had a box
they could have given us to play. You never did play down to Dauphine Theater, either, did you?
Dauphine Theater. I don't know whether we did or not. I'm not sure on that score.
